subject: Phased launch matrix + doc handback — decision and fallback lanes
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Dan Liu <dan.liu@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phased launch matrix + doc handback — decision and fallback lanes

Team —

Thanks for the sync earlier. I put together a first-pass phased launch matrix (attached) to reconcile the product timing constraints, docs ownership, and the minimum enableset we need to ship the first cohort of customers (SaaSCo included). TL;DR: there are three feasible launch lanes:

1) Narrow feature set, high enablement (docs + onboarding sessions) — target: 2026-11-15
2) Broader feature set, staged rollout (feature flags + canary) — target: 2026-12-06
3) Minimal GA with escape hatch (public API disabled, pilot-only) — target: 2027-01-10

Key asks:
- Ben: confirm infra readiness for lane 2 (canary auto-rollbacks + traffic slice).
- Marissa: confirm enablement capacity — how many live onboarding slots can we support in November vs December?
- Karthik: doc ownership handback — I proposed split by surface in the spreadsheet. Can you accept or propose edits?

Risk callouts in the sheet: SES quotas, model quantization artifacts in long-tail prompts, and a single regional dependency on eu-west for a partner integration.

If we can lock a lane by EOD Thursday (Sep 30) I can finalize the outreach plan for SaaSCo and get their acceptance on the pilot dates. Otherwise we default to lane 3 and plan a January GA.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Product Manager, Launch & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: phased_launch_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 7 tabs)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Dan Liu <dan.liu@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased launch matrix + doc handback — decision and fallback lanes

Priya —

Quick read: lane 2 is technically feasible assuming we get the autoscale knobs and canary policy in place. Two items I need to validate:

- Autoscale: current reserve capacity in dedicated pools can absorb 3x pilot concurrency for up to 12 hours; beyond that we need a temporary burst allocation request (ops will need a PO).
- Canary rollback: we have a working heuristics-based rollback (latency + error rate) but it needs a short runbook to avoid flapping (I can draft it).

I'll confirm the hard gating items by tomorrow lunch after I run a cap-exposure simulation. If the PO for burst is a blocker we should consider lane 1 or push lane 2 to Dec.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Dan Liu <dan.liu@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased launch matrix + doc handback — decision and fallback lanes

Adding enablement perspective:

- November (lane 1) — we have bandwidth for 8 live onboarding sessions (45–60m) plus 3 recorded deep dives. We can publish the enablement-outline.md and host internal rehearsal sessions.
- December (lane 2) — we can scale to ~20 live sessions if we add an extra enablement contractor and repurpose one of the customer success engineers for 6 weeks.

Docs: I skimmed the sheet and the split looks ok. I suggest we keep a single owner for the API quickstart (Karthik) and a single owner for deployment ops playbook (Ben). Other how-tos can be split by feature.

Action: I can firm up a rehearsal schedule and a public-facing FAQ if we lock lane by EOD Thu.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Enablement
Redwood Inference
Attachment: enablement-outline.md (markdown, 6 sections)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Phased launch matrix + doc handback — decision and fallback lanes

Thanks — I reviewed the spreadsheet and proposed small edits on tab 3 (API quickstart). High level:

- I'll take ownership of the quickstart and a minimal SDK sample for lane 1 (target: publish by 2026-11-01).
- Ben, I need any operational config snippets (canary flags, rollout gating thresholds) by Oct 8 so I can bake them into the ops playbook.
- Priya: for lane 2 we need language in the customer-facing docs about opt-in telemetry and quantization caveats; please confirm legal signoff cadence.

If we do lane 2 in December, I recommend a soft freeze on new surface additions Oct 15 so docs can catch up.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Docs & DevRel Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Dan Liu <dan.liu@saasco.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@platformpartner.io>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased launch matrix + doc handback — decision and fallback lanes

Priya / team —

Thanks for the clarity. From SaaSCo's POV the priority is predictable onboarding and a clear rollback/fallback path. We prefer lane 2 (December) if it means fewer operational surprises for our customers. If lane 2 requires a contract amendment for limited pilot capacity in November, we can entertain a short-term addendum.

Two asks from us:
- A date for when the public API will be enabled for our org (we need to schedule our integration sprint).
- A runbook for failover: how will we route traffic if eu-west has a transient outage?

Happy to take a 30m call to finalize dates.

—Dan
Dan Liu
Head of Integrations, SaaSCo
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Liu <dan.liu@saasco.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased launch matrix + doc handback — decision and fallback lanes

Folks —

Given the open blockers (burst PO, gating thresholds, legal signoff) and SaaSCo preference for December, recommend we: 

1) Lock lane 2 as our target (2026-12-06) with a soft commitment to SaaSCo.
2) Execute a short November pilot (limited cohort, lane 1 feature set) only if Ben confirms the burst PO by Oct 5.
3) Karthik & Marissa: handback deadlines — API quickstart by Nov 1; enablement materials for pilot by Nov 8.
4) Priya: draft a simple contract addendum for pilot capacity and share with legal for expedited review.

If everyone agrees I will send a one-page internal decision memo and coordinate a customer-facing date confirmation with Dan.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
